newsitem.title: NORWAY: Phillips shuts Ekofisk oilfield for repairs.
newsitem.headline: Phillips shuts Ekofisk oilfield for repairs.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum said on Monday it had stopped oil production at the 350,000 barrels per day North Sea Ekofisk field to carry out repairs to a pipeline.
The field was shut in at 0830 GMT on Sunday, spokeswoman Bjoerg Sandal told Reuters.
Crude output at third party fields -- British Petroleum's Gyda and Ula and Amoco's Valhall and Hod -- and the Statpipe gas line was uninterrupted by the shutdown, Sandal said.
Ekofisk production was stopped on January 14 for one week after a leak was discovered at one pipeline. Following that shutdown Phillips set up a regular inspection programme at the field.

"A inspection check on Sunday showed that the wall of one pipeline in the same area as the previous leak was too thin. There was no leak but we shutdown production immediately and are doing the repairs. We expect to be back up again sometime today," Sandal said.
